headline: Bill Ackman, founder of the hedge fund Pershing Square Capital Management, said the Federal Reserve might have made a mistake by raising interest rates, because AI spending may not respond to higher borrowing costs.
score_reason: Pool score kept: a prominent investor questions the Fed in public, but it is one opinion posted online.
importance_line: Anyone who borrows or saves is affected by whether the Fed's rate rise works, but Ackman's argument is an opinion posted on X and the Fed has not replied in the article.
summary: Stocktwits reports that Bill Ackman, founder of the hedge fund Pershing Square Capital Management, wrote on X that the Federal Reserve "might have just made a mistake", because the race to build "super intelligence" could keep companies and governments spending heavily on AI even as borrowing costs rise, so higher rates may not cool demand and could push prices up as interest costs spread through the economy. He was answering the Fed's recent decision to raise its benchmark interest rate by a quarter of a percentage point, to a range of 3.75% to 4%, after which Fed Chair Kevin Warsh said AI-related equipment and software investment had grown nearly 20% over the past year but that the timing and scale of its effect on supply remain uncertain; the article does not give the date of that decision.
notes: Reply story: Ackman answers the Fed's rate decision (date not given by Stocktwits); that decision was not carried in our recent editions. The date of the X post is not stated; the article was published after the Friday 16 Oct session.
